docs.title: TAVP: TED Autonomous Vehicle Project
docs.text: Welcome to the central documentation hub for TAVP. This project aims to develop a 1/10th scale autonomous racing car capable of navigating complex environments using Reinforcement Learning and Computer Vision.

docs.title: 🏎 Project Vision
docs.text: Our goal is to implement a robust autonomous stack on a Husqvarna Svartpilen-inspired RC platform, utilizing the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano for high-level AI and STM32 for low-level real-time control.

docs.title: 🏗 System Overview
docs.text:
graph TD
    subgraph "High-Level Processing (Jetson Orin Nano)"
        A[Camera/LIDAR] --> B{ROS2 Stack}
        B --> C[Vision Module]
        B --> D[RL Agent - SAC/PPO]
    end

    subgraph "Low-Level Control (STM32)"
        D -->|Serial/UART| E[Drive Controller]
        E --> F[Servo/Motor]
    end

    F -->|Telemetry| B

docs.title: 🔩 Hardware Architecture & Interface
docs.text: This document specifies the physical layer, wiring protocols, and power distribution for the TAVP Autonomous RC Car. The architecture follows a Distributed Control System (DCS) pattern, offloading real-time actuation to secondary microcontrollers.

docs.title: 🏗 High-Level System Topology
docs.text: The system is centered around the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, which serves as the primary compute node. Actuation is decoupled into two dedicated Arduino microcontrollers to ensure high-precision PWM timing and safety.

docs.title: 🛰 Component Specifications
docs.text: Component model Purpose Main Compute NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano ROS2 Node execution, AI Inference (SAC/PPO), LIDAR processing. Steering MCU Arduino Nano/Uno Real-time PWM generation for high-torque steering servo. Drive MCU Arduino Nano/Uno Speed control logic and H-Bridge direction switching. DC Motor Driver BTS7960 / IBT-2 High-current (43A) H-Bridge for drive motor traction. Power Source 3S/4S LiPo Battery 11.1V - 14.8V main power rail.

docs.title: 1. Steering Control (Arduino Node A)
docs.text:
To ensure smooth and jitter-free cornering, the Steering MCU maintains a constant 50Hz PWM signal. It receives steering angles from the Jetson via Serial at 115200 baud.

Arduino Pin Connection Logic/Function D9 Servo Signal PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) 5V / VIN External BEC Dedicated 5V/3A Power source GND Common Ground Reference ground for signal integrity

docs.title: 2. Traction Control (Arduino Node B)
docs.text:
The Drive MCU translates throttle commands into PWM duty cycles and manages the "Direction" pins for the H-Bridge motor driver.

Arduino Pin Connection Logic/Function D5 (PWM) RPWM / LPWM Speed Control (Duty Cycle) D4 L_EN / R_EN Enable pins for Motor Driver GND Common Ground Reference ground

docs.title: ⚡ Power Distribution & Safety
docs.text: Autonomous systems require stable power to prevent logic brownouts during high-current motor surges.

docs.title: 🔋 Power Rails
docs.text:
1. Logic Rail (5V): Powered by a 5V/5A Buck Converter. Feeds the Jetson and USB peripherals.
  2. Actuator Rail (Main Battery V): Direct connection to the Motor Driver.
  3. Servo Rail: Separate 6V regulator to prevent servo noise from affecting the Arduinos.

[!CAUTION] Common Ground Rule: All ground (GND) wires from the Jetson, Arduinos, Motor Driver, and Battery must be connected at a single point (Star Ground) to prevent ground loops and data corruption.

docs.title: 📡 Data Handshake Protocol
docs.text:
The communication between the Jetson (Master) and Arduinos (Slaves) follows a simple packet format to minimize latency:

Header Steering Throttle Checksum End $ -45.0 to 45.0 0 to 255 HEX \n

docs.title: 🔍 Udev Rule Configuration
docs.text:
To ensure the Jetson always identifies the correct Arduino for the correct task, we use persistent device naming:

# /etc/udev/rules.d/99-arduino-tavp.rules
SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="1a86", ATTRS{idProduct}=="7523", SYMLINK+="ttySteering"
SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="2341", ATTRS{idProduct}=="0043", SYMLINK+="ttyDrive"

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will help you set up the development environment for the TAVP Autonomous RC Car. Follow these steps to ensure your system is compatible with our ROS2 stack and hardware interface.

docs.title: 📋 Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure your machine (Host PC or Jetson) meets these requirements:

  • OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)
  • Middleware: ROS2 Humble Hawksbill
  • Python: 3.10+ (Note: Development on the documentation repo uses 3.12+)

docs.title: 1. System Workspace Setup
docs.text:
First, create a dedicated ROS2 workspace for the project.

# Create the workspace directory
mkdir -p ~/tavp_ws/src
cd ~/tavp_ws/src

# Clone the main documentation and sub-modules
git clone https://github.com/Tedu-Autonomous-RC-Car/rc_documentation.git

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text: We use a specific set of tools for AI inference and embedded communication.

docs.title: Python Libraries
docs.text:
Install the core requirements for the documentation and the Jetson control logic:

cd ~/tavp_ws/src/rc_documentation
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: ROS2 Packages
docs.text:
Install the necessary ROS2 drivers for our sensors and serial communication:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install ros-humble-joy ros-humble-teleop-twist-joy \
                 ros-humble-serial-driver ros-humble-v4l2-camera \
                 ros-humble-urg-node # If using Hokuyo LIDAR

docs.title: 3. Hardware Permissions (Critical)
docs.text:
To allow the Jetson to communicate with the two Arduinos without sudo every time, you must add your user to the dialout group.

sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER
# REBOOT your machine after running this!

docs.title: Identifying the Arduinos
docs.text:
Since we have two Arduinos (Steering and Drive), we use udev rules to fix their names. Create a new rules file:

sudo nano /etc/udev/rules.d/99-arduino.rules

Add these lines (Update the idProduct based on your specific Arduino models):

SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="1a86", SYMLINK+="ttySteering"
SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="2341", SYMLINK+="ttyDrive"

docs.title: 4. Building the Project
docs.text:
Once the dependencies are installed, build the workspace using colcon.

cd ~/tavp_ws
colcon build --symlink-install
source install/setup.bash

docs.title: 5. Documentation Development
docs.text:
If you are contributing to this documentation site, you can run a local preview server:

cd ~/tavp_ws/src/rc_documentation
mkdocs serve

Your live preview will be available at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: 🛠 Troubleshooting Common Issues
docs.text:
• Serial Port Busy: Ensure no other serial monitors (like Arduino IDE) are open.
  • ModuleNotFoundError: Ensure you have activated your Python virtual environment if you are using one.
  • Build Failure: Check that you have sourced your ROS2 installation: source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash.
